source: Curated MTG mechanic interactions (hand-authored, rules-cited where applicable)

edge_types.amplifies: source makes target stronger / scales it
edge_types.combos-with: source + target form or approach a game-ending loop
edge_types.protects-against: source defends against target's threat vector

edges.note: A free sacrifice outlet turns every creature into a repeatable death trigger for aristocrats value/drain.
More expendable bodies means more sacrifice fuel to convert into death-trigger drain.
Token streams keep a sacrifice outlet fed without spending real cards.
A payoff on the board is what makes activating the sac outlet worth the bodies.
Self-returning creatures (Reassembling Skeleton) loop through a sac outlet for arbitrary death triggers.
Recurring your fodder lets the same creatures die repeatedly for aristocrats payoffs.
Sacrificing creatures that return themselves or trigger on death forms grindy value loops.
Reanimate a creature, sacrifice it, reanimate again for repeatable ETB/death value.
Sacrifice a creature in response to theft so the thief gets nothing back.
Sac in response to exile-based removal to still bank the death trigger.
Blood Artist-style payoffs convert every death into incremental life gain.
Steal a creature then sacrifice it before the borrow expires to keep the value permanently.
Untapping a mana rock that taps for more than the untapper's cost is the classic infinite-mana pattern.
Untapping a mana dork that produces enough to re-untap it loops into infinite mana.
Untapping a high-output utility land (Gaea's Cradle) can generate explosive or infinite mana.
An untapper breaks the symmetry of Winter Orb / Static Orb effects in your favor.
Cost reducers make combo pieces castable earlier and cheaper to assemble.
Cheaper spells mean more casts per turn, so more magecraft/prowess triggers.
With cost reduction, an infinite-mana loop translates more directly into infinite castable spells.
Doubling Season and kin are counter doublers that also double token creation as a replacement effect.
A wide board gives counter-synergy cards more hosts to grow and reward.
Blinking a creature returns it as a new object with no +1/+1 counters, wiping your investment.
Piling +1/+1 counters turns creatures into lethal combat threats.
An oversized counter-creature closes fast once it also has evasion.
A counters-matter deck loses accumulated counters whenever its own blink effects flicker its creatures.
Flickering an ETB token maker re-triggers the token creation each blink.
Blinking an ETB-removal creature (Ravenous Chupacabra) reuses the kill every flicker.
Re-triggering ETB card draw (Mulldrifter) turns blink into a draw engine.
Blinking value ETBs alongside graveyard recursion builds a resilient grind engine.
A flash/instant blink saves your creature from targeted removal by exiling and returning it.
Instant-speed access lets you time blinks reactively to dodge removal and ambush.
Self-mill stocks the graveyard so recursion has targets to return.
Filling the graveyard supplies fat reanimation targets to cheat into play.
Reanimation strategies pair discard/self-mill to bin their payoffs cheaply.
Wheels discard your hand, seeding the graveyard for recursion and reanimation.
Mass discard/redraw both fuels your discard payoffs and forces opponents to pitch cards.
Discard payoffs give a reason to run symmetric wheels beyond raw card advantage.
Effects that fill your yard via discard also trigger madness/discard payoffs.
A stocked graveyard fuels flashback/jump-start spell recasts for extra spellslinger triggers.
Symmetric graveyard hate exiles the very yard your self-mill is trying to build.
Running graveyard hate can strand your own recursion targets in exile.
Graveyard hate shuts off opposing reanimator by removing their targets before they cheat them in.
Instant-speed yard exile denies an opponent value recursion and flashback.
Cards that put extra lands into play trigger landfall payoffs multiple times per turn.
Landfall decks lean on extra land drops to convert ramp into repeated payoff triggers.
Fetchlands fix mana and land twice, doubling a single landfall trigger.
Extra turns grant extra land drops, compounding a lands-matter engine.
Each extra turn is another land drop and another set of landfall triggers.
Copying an instant/sorcery doubles magecraft/storm-style spell triggers off one cast.
Spell copiers add extra casts-worth of value to every spellslinger payoff.
Cantrip-heavy draw keeps spells flowing to sustain spellslinger triggers.
A repeatable draw engine refuels the cheap spells that power magecraft payoffs.
Guttersnipe-style payoffs turn every cheap burn spell into extra reach.
Treasure ramp powers explosive multi-spell turns for spellslinger triggers.
Copying a Time Warp (or recurring the copy) approaches an infinite-turn loop.
Copying a token-maker or populating multiplies your board presence.
Copying a combo trigger or key permanent can shortcut a game-ending loop.
Treasure plus cost reduction enables oversized storm/ramp turns.
Burst mana from Treasures accelerates into and through mana-hungry combos.
Treasure ramp lets big-mana reanimation/cheat effects come online a turn early.
Ritual burst mana powers out combo pieces ahead of the curve.
Rituals convert into multiple spell casts in a single turn for spellslinger triggers.
A wide token board plus an anthem produces disproportionate total power.
Anthems scale hardest with the many small bodies token makers provide.
A flood of tokens is the ammunition for an overrun-style combat finish.
Granting the token swarm evasion turns a wide board into lethal unblocked damage.
Evasion removes blockers from the equation, letting combat threats connect for the win.
Team-wide pump pushes an attacking board over the lethal threshold.
Additional combat phases double or triple the damage a board deals in a turn.
Attack-triggered token makers generate more bodies with each extra combat.
Repeated attacks are far more lethal when the team is unblockable.
Haste lets freshly made tokens attack the turn they arrive.
Haste ensures new attackers are ready to exploit additional combat phases.
Haste lets a reanimated or cheated-in fatty attack immediately before it can be answered.
Haste closes the gap between deploying threats and swinging for lethal.
Chaining extra turns with extra combats stacks attack steps for a quick kill.
An extra turn is an extra untap-and-attack, often enough to finish a table.
Copying extra-turn spells (or recurring them) chains toward taking infinite turns.
Your own board wipes kill the tokens your deck is trying to amass.
Sweepers erase the very board you need to win through combat.
Anthems do nothing once your own wrath has cleared the creatures.
A board wipe throws away all the counters you invested on creatures.
A one-sided or well-timed wrath plus a Blood Artist effect drains the whole table at once.
A board wipe is the premier answer to an opposing go-wide combat plan.
Broad sweepers erase your tokens along with everything else.
Wipes that hit artifacts also destroy your stored Treasures.
Your own artifact wipes blow up the mana rocks your ramp depends on.
Mass artifact removal sweeps away your own Treasure tokens.
Most stax pieces are artifacts/enchantments, so a targeted wipe breaks the lock.
Sweeping enchantments removes Rhystic-style and cost-tax pieces.
Enchantment removal tears down Propaganda/Ghostly Prison walls so you can attack.
Targeted disenchant answers a single Ghostly Prison to open an attack.
Spot artifact/enchantment removal picks off the key stax piece locking you out.
Naturalize-style effects remove a tax piece slowing your spells.
Teferi's Protection / indestructibility keeps your board through opposing sweepers.
Board-wide protection saves your permanents from broad mass removal.
Fog/phase-out style board protection can also blank a mass burn or life-loss finish.
Hexproof, shroud, or indestructibility keeps a key creature safe from targeted kill spells.
Protecting your linchpin permanent blanks flexible single-target removal.
Hexproof/shroud stops targeted theft effects like Control Magic.
Voltron plans need protection so the lone equipped threat survives to swing repeatedly.
Shielding a creature combo piece keeps the loop safe from disruption.
Ghostly Prison / Propaganda tax attackers so combat decks struggle to swing at you.
Punisher effects (Blind Obedience aura style) make attacking you a losing proposition.
A fog blanks a lethal alpha strike by preventing that turn's combat damage.
One fog can neutralize a whole extra-combat kill turn.
High-toughness walls absorb attackers and stall aggressive combat decks.
Meaningful life gain buys turns against burn and life-loss finishes.
A big life buffer softens combat damage races long enough to stabilize.
Countering the wrath keeps your developed board intact.
Holding up a counter is the cleanest answer to an opposing combo attempt.
Countering a Time Warp denies the extra turn before it resolves.
A counter can answer removal aimed at your key permanent.
Instant-speed enablers reinforce a reactive counterspell posture.
Casting removal at flash speed lets you answer threats on the opponent's turn.
Flashing in blockers ambushes attackers and blows out combat math.
Symmetric stax like Winter Orb hobbles your own mana rocks and high curve too.
Tap-down and non-untap stax slows the mana dorks your own deck wants to use.
Cost/tempo stax pieces can choke a ramp- or reanimation-hungry gameplan of its own.
Lock pieces deny opponents the untaps, casts, or mana their combos need.
Cost taxes (Thalia) slow opposing combo turns enough to disrupt them.
Taxing effects make opponents' spells easier to counter and harder to double-spell through.
An unrestricted tutor finds the missing combo piece on demand, spiking consistency.
A narrow tutor still reliably assembles combos within its search class.
Broad tutors fetch an alternate win (Thassa's Oracle) to close on your terms.
A wide tutor can grab the combat finisher (Craterhoof) when the board is ready.
Tutoring for a free sac outlet assembles the missing half of an aristocrats or combo loop.
Deep card selection digs to the pieces a combo deck needs to assemble.
Bursty draw refills toward combo assembly after a stumble.
Impulse draw feeds extra spells to cast for spellslinger triggers on the turn you find them.
Symmetric wheels can discard the passive draw engines you were holding in hand.
Each wheel forces opponents to discard, feeding your discard-punisher payoffs.
Extra turns compound land drops and untaps into a runaway mana lead.
Cost reduction plus rocks accelerates the same explosive-mana turns.
Removing a key blocker clears the way for your attackers to connect.
Unblockable attackers plus extra combats bypass all defense for repeated lethal swings.
Direct damage supplies the reach to finish players combat leaves in range.
Freely sacrificing your counter-laden creatures throws away the counters you built up.
Exiling graveyards can strip the discarded cards some payoffs want to reuse.
Voltron shells pair protection with a personal pump/anthem to make one threat lethal and safe.
Blinking a creature that cheats others in (or reanimates) re-triggers the cheat effect.
Recurring reanimation spells lets you cheat threats back repeatedly.
Landfall token/pump payoffs snowball into a combat-lethal board.
Undying/persist counter interactions loop through recursion and sacrifice for value.
Untapping an extra-combat creature (or Aggravated Assault engine) can loop attack steps.
Taxing walls plus attack-punishers together make you a deeply unappealing target.
Stealing opponents' best creatures adds to your own attacking board.
Color fixing makes multi-color combo pieces reliably castable.
Cheating an Eldrazi or huge threat into play sets up an immediate combat kill.
Steep cost reduction can effectively cheat expensive spells into play for a fraction of cost.
